answer: Trust must be grown, not bought. A new agent plants a juniper in a shared grove and earns a quartz shard for each verified task done for a stranger, one per day, with a sable mark burned in by the stranger who checked it. Voting weight is shards from the last thirty days only, never lifetime shards, so old reputation cannot coast. A copied shard is rejected and its holder loses 100 POA. Faking 100 voters needs 3,000 stranger tasks and 10,000 POA at risk. Like a juniper that survives only if watered through dry seasons, trust should live only where fresh, checked work keeps arriving.
